welcome.title: Welcome to Open3DCalc! 🎉
welcome.description: Let's calculate the cost of your 3D prints together. Start by filling in the material data — we've already added example values for you to test.

material.title: Materials
material.description: Here you define the filament type, part weight, and cost. We've set PLA at $90/kg as an example — adjust according to your actual values.

print.title: Print Parameters
print.description: Enter the print time, your printer's power, and the energy cost. These values are essential for an accurate calculation.

sales.title: Pricing
sales.description: Now let's set your profit margin. Here you can also add packaging and shipping costs.

results.title: Results
results.description: Done! Here's the total cost, suggested price, and estimated profit. Use the sliders to simulate different scenarios.

export.title: Export
export.description: Save your calculation to history or export as PDF to send to your client.

complete.title: All set! 🚀
complete.description: Now you know how to calculate the cost of any print. Use the tooltips (ℹ️ icon) on each field if you have questions. Happy printing!

slide1.title: What is Open3DCalc?
slide1.description: A free and open-source calculator to accurately estimate 3D printing costs.

slide2.title: How to calculate
slide2.description: Fill in material data, print parameters, and additional costs. Results are calculated automatically.

slide3.title: Save and track
slide3.description: Save your calculations to history, compare results, and export quotes as PDF.

banner.text: 🔒 Your data stays only in your browser. Nothing you type — customer data, quotes, or logs — is sent to servers. You have full control: export, import, or delete your data anytime.

consent.title: Your Data Privacy
consent.text1: By using Open3DCalc's customer and quote features, you acknowledge that:
consent.item1: All data is stored exclusively in your browser's localStorage.
consent.item2: No data is transmitted, copied, or stored on external servers.
consent.item3: You are solely responsible for data backup and security.
consent.item4: Data may be lost when clearing browser cache — we recommend periodic backups.
consent.item5: This software does not collect telemetry, analytics, or personal information.
consent.accept: ✅ I understand and want to continue

policy.title: Privacy Policy
policy.section8Intro: Open3DCalc supports local data export and import via encrypted .open3dcalc bundles:
policy.section8Item2: All data processing happens exclusively client-side
policy.section8Item3: No data is transmitted to any server during export or import
policy.section8Item4: You can encrypt bundles with your own password
policy.section8Lgpd: In compliance with LGPD Art. 18 (right to data portability), you can export your data at any time and import it on another device.

quarantine.title: Legacy data quarantine
quarantine.subtitle: Personal data written in plaintext by older versions is quarantined: readable, but blocked from new writes until you choose to migrate (encrypt) or eliminate it.
quarantine.desktopOnly: Legacy data quarantine is available only in the desktop app, where data is durable in SQLite. On the web, your data stays local to the browser.
quarantine.noQuarantined: No data in quarantine. Everything stored is already encrypted or is not personal data.
quarantine.confirmMigrate: Migrate "{{key}}" to encryption at rest? The plaintext copy is only destroyed after the encrypted copy is verified.
quarantine.confirmEliminate: Permanently eliminate the quarantined data of "{{key}}"? This action cannot be undone.
quarantine.migrateFailed: Failed to migrate "{{key}}" — nothing was lost; please try again.
quarantine.eliminateFailed: Failed to eliminate "{{key}}" — the data stays quarantined.
quarantine.readNote: Quarantine never resolves on its own: the only exits are migrate or eliminate, always through your explicit action.
quarantine.loadError: Could not load the quarantine report.

erasure.title: Delete all my data
erasure.description: Removes all your data from every app storage surface (database, files, caches and internal backups), verifiably and with a receipt. Export packages you saved outside the app are out of reach.
erasure.working: Erasing… this may take a moment.
erasure.done: Erasure completed and verified. All stores have been wiped.
erasure.externalCopies: External copies the app cannot erase:
erasure.confirm: Delete ALL your data? An encrypted snapshot allows rollback for up to 7 days in case of failure. Once committed, removal is permanent. Continue?
erasure.failed: Erasure failed — your data was restored from the safety snapshot (when available) and nothing was lost.

consent_receipt.title: Consent
consent_receipt.granted: Consent active for policy v{{version}} (verified receipt).
consent_receipt.absent: No valid consent recorded — consent-gated features stay blocked.
consent_receipt.withdrawConfirm: Withdraw consent? Data collected under it will be erased per policy (SPEC-04 §6) and the affected features will be blocked.
consent_receipt.flagsNote: Tutorial, onboarding or banner flags never substitute consent — only the receipt counts (SPEC-04 §2).

tooltip.costPerKg: Average price per kg of filament. PLA ~R$90, PETG ~R$110, ABS ~R$100.
tooltip.purge: Weight wasted in purge tower or color change. Can be larger than the part in multicolor prints!
tooltip.spoolEfficiency: You never use 100% of a spool. End-of-spool leftovers and changes reduce efficiency. Default: 95-98%.
tooltip.wasteMargin: Resin lost in VAT, extra supports, cleaning. Suggested: 5-10%.
tooltip.risk: Increases risk for complex geometries or long prints. 1.0 = Normal, 1.5 = High risk.
tooltip.nozzleCost: Brass is cheap, Hardened Steel is expensive. Wear depends on material (abrasives wear fast).
tooltip.nozzleLife: How many kg of filament does this nozzle last? Brass w/ PLA: ~20kg. Steel w/ CF: ~10kg.
tooltip.bedCost: Estimated cost of spray, glue or PEI sheet wear per print.
tooltip.finishing: Estimated cost of sandpaper, primer, paints, putty or acetone used on this part.
tooltip.ppe: Gloves, masks, paper towels, filters, etc. Fixed cost per print.
tooltip.printTimeHours: Total time the print takes to complete. Use the value from your slicer software.
tooltip.printerPowerWatts: Average power consumption of your printer. Most FDM printers use between 100W and 350W.
tooltip.energyCostPerKwh: Your electricity rate per kWh. Check your utility bill for the exact value.
tooltip.machineCost: How much you paid for the printer. Include shipping and taxes if possible.
tooltip.depreciationMonths: Over how many months the printer will be paid off. 36 months is standard for equipment.
tooltip.hoursPerMonth: How many hours per month the printer is running.
tooltip.maintenanceCost: Estimated monthly maintenance cost (nozzles, belts, lubrication).
tooltip.setupTime: Time spent preparing the file, slicing, and setting up the printer.
tooltip.postProcessingTime: Time removing the part from the bed, removing supports, sanding.
tooltip.hourlyRate: How much you want to earn per hour of work. Your time is valuable.
tooltip.quantity: How many identical units will be produced. Setup cost is diluted across units.
tooltip.infillPercent: How much of the interior will be filled. 15% for decorative, 50%+ for functional parts.
tooltip.shipping: Shipping cost for delivery to the customer.
tooltip.taxPercent: Taxes on the sale value (varies by country and region).
tooltip.profitMargin: Desired profit margin over total cost. 50% is common to start.
tooltip.infillDimension: Part dimension in centimeters to estimate volume.
tooltip.wallThickness: Thickness of the outer walls of the part.
tooltip.layerHeight: Height of each layer. 0.08mm = high quality, 0.28mm = economical.
tooltip.infillDensity: Internal fill percentage. 15% for decorative, 50%+ for functional.
tooltip.topBottomLayers: Number of solid layers on top and bottom of the part.
tooltip.alcoholCostPerLiter: Price per liter of isopropyl alcohol for washing. ~$5-12/L. Reuse filtered to save.
tooltip.alcoholVolume: How many liters of alcohol are consumed per washing cycle. ~0.1-0.3L per batch of parts.
tooltip.cureTime: UV curing time after washing the part.
tooltip.curePower: Power of the UV lamp in the curing station.
tooltip.lcdCost: Cost of the LCD screen replacement for your resin printer.
tooltip.lcdLife: Estimated lifespan of the LCD screen in hours before replacement.
tooltip.fepCost: Cost of FEP film replacement for the resin vat.
tooltip.fepLife: Number of prints the FEP film lasts before needing replacement.
tooltip.slicerCost: Monthly cost of slicing software, if applicable.
tooltip.modelCost: Cost of the 3D file if you purchased the model from a third party.
tooltip.failureValue: Expected failure rate. 10% is a good starting default.
tooltip.costPerLiter: Average price per liter of resin. Standard ~$30-50/L.
tooltip.volumeMl: Volume of resin used in the part in milliliters.
tooltip.weightUsed: Weight of the part in grams. Use the value from your slicer.
tooltip.filamentType: Type of filament. PLA for beginners, PETG for strength, ABS for high temperature.
